steps.text: Spread cucumber and onion slices onto a large platter; season with salt on both sides. Let rest for 30 minutes, then drain in a colander and squeeze to remove excess moisture. Blot dry with paper towels.
To make the dressing: Stir sour cream, sugar, vinegar, dill, and parsley together in a large bowl.
Gently fold cucumber and onion slices into dressing until coated. Cover and refrigerate, at least 3 hours to overnight.

raw_recipe.headline: Gurkensalat (German Cucumber Salad)
raw_recipe.description: This chilled German cucumber salad, known as gurkensalat, is made with sliced cucumbers and onions marinated in sour cream, vinegar, and dill.

video.description: Do your German grandmother proud and make the classic cucumber salad, fresh and delicious, just as she did! The great flavors are all due to a couple of special techniques. First, salting cucumbers and onions to help them release their liquid and distill their flavors. After squeezing excess moisture from the cukes, stir them with a creamy mixture of sour cream, sugar, vinegar, dill and parsley and then follow this crucial step: chill overnight. Give the salad a bright garnish of paprika and don’t be surprised if you eat it all in one sitting!

review.reviewBody: We must all have the same German grandma. I have been eating this salad for years. It is one of my favorites. Grandma used chives instead of dill and she also smashed a clove of garlic and added it with the onions, cucumbers and salt.

I'm German and this recipe was wonderful with a few changes: I reduced the sugar to 1 tsp and added the green parts of 2 sliced scallions at the end instead of the onions. Question: the salad tasted great but the sour cream mixture turned frothy when I served it. Any idea why?

Like many others, I have had this dish since I was a kid and loved it. My salting technique differs a little though. After peeling and slicing, the cucumbers go into a colander. I then salt them generously with kosher salt (don't bother measuring), then place a bowl of water on top to squeeze them for an hour. I then rinse the excess salt off and dry them with paper towels. The purpose of this step is not to remove water (like you do with zucchini) but acid. Yes, they do end up limp. But if you belch up cucumbers for hours after eating them, like I do, you'll appreciate the difference. Also, as long as the salad's cold, the 8 hours or overnight in the fridge is probably unnecessary. Doesn't hurt though. Lastly, the paprika garnish is just to add a little color. An entire teaspoon, unless you're using a very wide bowl, is probably overkill.

Cucumber salads tend to be somewhat the same. With this recipe I was interested in the impact the addition of paprika would have on the taste. I made it per the instructions but left out the sugar because I don't like it sweet. In spite of not adding the sugar it seemed the paprika did add some sweetness of its own. I enjoyed this immensely and would make it again.
My mom always made a salad like this. (she was from Germany). I've been making it too, but with parsley and chives and a tiny dab of yellow mustard. It's a nice and refeshing summer salad.

Tasty! Per reviewers, cut sugar by 1/2. Would probably cut it a bit further next time, as well as add a little bit more vinegar, as I wanted it less sweet and more tangy. The sour cream was a nice touch that C was skeptical of but ended up really liking! Made it about 2 hours ahead of time, in accordance with reviews that said it gets mushy if it sits overnight, and used an English cucumber.

I used mayo and sour cream half and half and I didn't end up using all the sauce on the cucumbers because I don't like it soupy. I also left the veggies in a colander over the sink for 3 minutes to drain
Good recipe, tried pickled red onion this time, a nice variation but the original is excellent. I may put less sugar next time. 2 tbsp seems a lot.

Only thing I did different was I salted all the slices while in water, rinsed well, then used my salad spinner to get as much liquid out as I could. (Used a mandolin to slice onions and cucumber very thin too.)

Delicious! I went with a heaping four cups of thinly sliced cucumbers since ‘two cucumbers’ wasn’t very specific. One large sweet onion sliced thin. Used two tsp kosher salt for getting the water to release from the cukes. Did a double batch of the sour cream mixture, so 1.5 cups sour cream and double other items except sugar. After reading the reviews I cut the sugar in half and glad I did as we don’t care for super sweet dishes. Used fresh fern dill, skipped the paprika, added .5 tsp coarse pepper, but I think you could go a full teaspoon. Will be making this again.

I made this for a party and it was commended! I left off the paprika as I didn't have any, no other ingredient changes. I made the sour cream mixture and sliced the cucumbers a night in advance, but mixed it all together about an hour before the party to keep the cucumbers from becoming too soggy. Will make again!
Sugar isn't necessary in my opinion but great summer side dish with our garden cucumbers
Lovely
Changed nothing, family loved it, super refreshing!
It creates a yummy result but is also a recipe that may require you to buy some ingredients and make this first attempt an investment. I love this side dish/salad.
Ir reminded me of the way my grandmother in PA made it in the summers with cucumbers and onions from their garden.
I’m not German but Grandma made this a lot in the summer, and it was my favorite dish! Can’t wait to try it again!
Wow!!!! Absolutely delicious way to use up cucumbers.

A friend gifted us some extra cukes from her garden, and I was planning to make an Italian-style tomato and cucumber salad with them, but then I remembered the cucumber salad I used to have when I studied in Austria that had a sour cream-based dressing. A quick search pulled up this recipe, and while it's not exactly the same, it's still delicious! My husband loved it too. I did reduce the sugar slightly (made a 1.5× recipe and kept the sugar amount at 2 Tbsp), and while the dressing by itself was quite sweet, the salt on the vegetables balanced it out nicely once they were dressed. I'll definitely be making this one again.
Less sugar! But good otherwise!
